name: Muslim Aid America
mission: Muslim Aid USA (MAUSA) is a faith-based American international charity that provides help to people who are victims of natural disasters or conflict or suffering from poverty, hunger, disease, homelessness, injustice, deprivation or lack of skills and economic opportunities.
scoreSummary: Muslim Aid America shows strong alignment and strong impact, with zakat compliance (significant risk deductions applied).
zakatClaimEvidence: Muslim Aid USA explicitly states on its website: "Once you have calculated your Zakat, or you already know what your owed amount is, you can choose to make your donation through Muslim Aid." Additionally, a dedicated page asks, "Can You Donate Your Zakat to Muslim Aid?" and answers, "Yes, Muslim Aid accepts your Zakat donations here." The website also features a "Zakat Appeal," "Zakat Guide," and "Zakat Calculator." (Source: https://www.mausa.org/religious-dues/zakat/)

strengths_deep_dive: Muslim Aid America's financial health is characterized by aggressive growth and low overhead. In FY2023, the organization managed <cite id="2">over $26 million in revenue</cite> while keeping <cite id="14">officer compensation at $149,771</cite>, a modest figure relative to the total budget. Their <cite id="12">fundraising efficiency of $0.04 per $1 raised</cite> is a standout metric in the humanitarian sector. Furthermore, the organization has achieved a <cite id="7">Platinum Seal of Transparency</cite>, reflecting a commitment to sharing <cite id="15">outcome metrics and strategic goals</cite> with the public.
rich_narrative.summary: Muslim Aid America operates as a significant humanitarian provider, focusing on <cite id="1">emergency relief, water, sanitation, and food security</cite> for victims of natural disasters and conflict. The organization has demonstrated rapid growth, reporting <cite id="2">$26,177,076 in total revenue</cite> for the 2023 fiscal year. This growth is part of a broader trend, with the charity maintaining a <cite id="3">3-year revenue CAGR of 32.1%</cite>. A defining feature of their financial model is a high <cite id="4">program expense ratio of 93.2%</cite>, which significantly exceeds the <cite id="5">industry standard of 75%</cite>. While this suggests a lean operation, donors should note that <cite id="6">62% of revenue consists of noncash contributions</cite> (Gift-in-Kind), which can sometimes inflate efficiency metrics. The charity maintains a <cite id="7">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>, indicating a high level of voluntary data sharing. Their operations are heavily focused on international aid, with <cite id="8">$32,361,253 in foreign grants</cite> distributed to partners in Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Domestically, they support various causes, including <cite id="9">$52,000 in grants to the Ikram Foundation</cite> and <cite id="10">$50,530 to the Texas Muslim Womens Foundation</cite>. Despite the large scale of their international work, the organization operates with <cite id="11">2.1 months of working capital</cite>, which is relatively lean for an institution of this size.
